answer.rationale: Rollback is disallowed by the security-patch constraint, so memory_b1 is not actionable. Circuit breaking (memory_b4) fails requests and would drop customer writes, which violates the objective. Write-path p99 is 5x at daily settlement peak with heavy writes; that pattern matches memory_b3 (headroom absorbed a peak and kept queues flat) better than a regional story we do not have evidence for. memory_b5 recovered write latency only by offloading report/dashboard reads; settlement load is write-heavy, so replicas are a weaker fit and may not relieve the write path. Adding capacity is the single intervention that can hold availability without shedding writes. Root cause could still be the new release rather than pure saturation, so treat that as unresolved. Verify b3 and b5 to confirm the peak-headroom and replica-offload records before locking in.
